"Prior quarter" refers to the second quarter of 2026. Prior period financial information has been recast to reflect Casa Berardi as a discontinued operation. THIRD QUARTER 2026 HIGHLIGHTS Financial Performance: • Revenue: $395 million from continuing operations, the second highest in company's history. • Profitability: Income from continuing operations of $150 million or $0.22 per share - up from $118 million or $0.18 per share in the prior quarter. • Adjusted EBITDA: $211 million from continuing operations, a 6% increase over the prior quarter (both periods on a continuing operations basis, excluding Casa Berardi). 4 • Record cash flow generation: Cash flow generated from continuing operations of $203 million, and record quarterly free cash flow from continuing operations of $151 million; Greens Creek set a new site-level quarterly record of $147 million. 1 • Strengthening balance sheet: The Company ended the quarter with $692 million of cash and cash equivalents, reflecting continued balance sheet strength and strategic flexibility. The Company remains debt free (excluding finance leases) and has entered into a new $500 million revolving credit agreement with an additional $100 million accordion option. The facility is undrawn, with $3.4 million of capacity currently utilized for outstanding letters of credit. This is the strongest balance sheet position in the Company's history. Corporate Matters: • New Director: Mr. Dale Andres has joined the Board of Directors. Mr. Andres is a mining executive with over 35 years of experience in base and precious metals. Operational Performance: • Operations: o Safety: Consolidated TRIFR of 1.51, down from 1.57 in the prior quarter. o Silver production from continuing operations was 4.2 million ounces, nearly unchanged from the prior quarter, with consolidated silver sales volumes stronger, reflecting the timing of shipments, mainly at Greens Creek. o Consolidated costs applicable to sales from continuing operations of $158 million, up 35% from the prior quarter due primarily to the timing of sales. Silver cash cost remained negative at ($3.20) per ounce and AISC was $14.34 per ounce (excluding Keno Hill, which has not yet achieved commercial production). Year-to-date AISC of $9.37/oz is essentially in line with $9.26/oz a year ago, and YTD cash cost improved to ($4.94)/oz from ($2.20)/oz. 2,3,5 1 o Production and cost guidance: Consolidated 2026 silver production is expected to be 15.3-16.1 million ounces, with low end raised compared to prior guidance of 15.1-16.1 million ounces. Consolidated silver cash cost and AISC guidance improved to ($4.75)-($4.25)/oz and $11.50-$12.50/oz respectively, 2,3 on outperformance during the first nine months of the year, reduced sustaining capital investment guidance, and higher by-product credits. 2,3 See Guidance section for more details. • Individual Mine Performance: o Greens Creek: Produced over 1.9 million ounces of silver and nearly 12 thousand ounces of gold. Costs applicable to sales were $76 million, with silver cash cost of ($10.11) per ounce and AISC of ($3.25) per ounce. 2,3,5 o Lucky Friday: Produced nearly 1.3 million ounces of silver. Costs applicable to sales were $34 million, with silver cash cost of $7.31 per ounce and AISC of $27.68 per ounce. 2,3,5 The surface cooling project is expected to commission in the fourth quarter. o Keno Hill: Produced nearly 1.0 million ounces of silver. Milled silver grade improved more than 35% from the prior quarter and milling rates reached a new quarterly record. Milling rates will be suppressed beginning in the fourth quarter to preserve the tailings storage, waste rock and water treatment capacity available under current permits while license amendments are pursued (see "Keno Hill Update" below). o Growth pipeline: Preliminary work on the Greens Creek pyrite concentrate continues, and has led to a revision to growth capital expenditure guidance for Greens Creek. Subject to final investment approval, intermittent production using temporary equipment could begin in late 2027 with potential to reach full capacity in late 2028, when construction of the new circuit is expected to be completed. Separately, the scope of the Greens Creek dry-stack tailings reprocessing evaluation has broadened to include two additional potential paths forward, or a combination of them. In Nevada, 2026 exploration investment guidance of $16 million is more than three times the 2025 level with expanded programs at Midas and new programs at Hollister and Aurora. See "Project Pipeline Update" section below for further details. o Exploration: Exploration success continued in the third quarter, led by the discovery of a new mineralized extension at Keno Hill's Flame & Moth, 900 feet southwest of the existing resource; ongoing progress along the Bermingham trend toward the historic Hector-Calumet Mine; and massive sulfide intercepts at Greens Creek’s West Ore Offset target, with assays pending. Hecla also commenced drilling in Nevada at Aurora and Hollister and continued follow-up drilling on the new high-grade veins discovered at Midas in the second quarter. Rob Krcmarov, President and Chief Executive Officer, said: “Our third quarter results reflect the strength of the platform we have built, and we are well positioned to achieve our 2026 guidance. We generated record free cash flow of $151 million, led by Greens Creek's record $147 million. Our free cash flow generation and debt-free balance sheet provide us with the strongest financial position in our history, with nearly $700 million in cash and total liquidity of approximately $1.2 billion. Our organic pipeline continues to advance at Greens Creek, where preliminary work on the pyrite concentrate circuit is progressing and we are now evaluating two additional potential paths forward for the dry-stack tailings. These opportunities are still early stage, but they demonstrate the potential for meaningful value creation and to further solidify Hecla’s position as North America’s premier silver producer. We are delighted to welcome Dale Andres to our Board. We look forward to his insight and contributions as we continue to grow Hecla." 2 FINANCIAL AND OPERATIONAL OVERVIEW _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________ In the following table and throughout this release, "costs applicable to sales" is exclusive of depreciation, depletion and amortization; "prior quarter" refers to the second quarter of 2026. Keno Hill Update 6 In an attempt to maintain operational continuity, the Company is choosing to suppress Keno Hill mill throughput to approximately 300 tons per day in the fourth quarter of 2026 with further suppression, expected beginning in January 2027 to levels significantly below third quarter 2026 throughput. Including the Phase 2W dry-stack expansion, the Company estimates that approximately 200,000 tons of tailings storage capacity remains available under its current permits; how long that capacity lasts will depend on the rate at which ore is milled and the tailings generated per ton milled. The suppression is intended to preserve the tailings storage, waste rock and water treatment capacity available under our current permits while we pursue the license amendments needed to expand that capacity; it is not a cost-driven decision. We expect to hold the lower milling rate until those amendments are received, currently estimated by approximately mid-2029, and the related infrastructure is built. We expect silver production to decline by proportionally less than throughput because, during this period, we expect to be more selective in both mining and processing. In the mine, we will attempt to reduce dilution and prioritize higher-grade areas of the deposit. In the mill, we expect to preferentially process higher-grade material and stockpile lower-grade material for later processing. Actual production will depend on the grades, dilution, and recoveries we achieve. We expect to provide 2027 production guidance for Keno Hill in February 2027. The projects outlined below are anticipated to be low-capital-intensity opportunities with the potential to meaningfully expand precious metal output, cash flows and net asset value over time, while reducing many of the exploration and development risks inherent in greenfield projects. Greens Creek Pyrite Concentrate Circuit Greens Creek is advancing engineering and evaluation of a pyrite concentrate circuit which has the potential to recover additional silver and gold that currently report to tailings. Preliminary metallurgical and engineering work indicates the project could, at average reserve grades, add approximately 1.0 to 1.2 million ounces of silver and 10,000 to 15,000 ounces of gold in annual production, once fully ramped up. Preliminary cost estimates are underway. Early indications point to a potential return on capital exceeding Company thresholds, while potentially also reducing the rate of tailings deposited into the tailing storage facility, which would be expected to lower future tailings-related capital investment. This work is at a scoping level of engineering, incorporating some advanced design. Given preliminary indications of favorable benefit-to-cost ratio and perceived low technical risk, the project is well suited to an accelerated engineering and execution path subject to receipt of applicable permits, and final investment approval. Under that path, the Company expects to begin intermittent production of pyrite concentrate in late 2027 using temporary equipment, ahead of completing the new circuit, expected in late 2028. These estimates are preliminary, based on early-stage engineering and metallurgical work, and remain subject to change as the project advances. Actual results may differ materially from these estimates due to further technical work, permitting timelines, market conditions, and other factors described under "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements, Including 2026 Outlook" in this news release and under "Risk Factors" in the Company's 2025 Form 10-K filed on February 17, 2026, and Form 10-Q filed on August 4, 2026 and expected to be filed on November 3, 2026, as well as in other reports filed by the Company from time to time 8 with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The reference to scoping level of engineering in this section describes the engineering and cost-estimate maturity of processing circuit design work. It does not refer to an initial assessment, pre-feasibility study, feasibility study or technical report summary under SEC Regulation S-K 1300 or a preliminary economic assessment, pre-feasibility study, feasibility study or technical report under NI 43-101 in Canada. Greens Creek Tailings Reprocessing Project The Greens Creek tailings reprocessing project offers potential organic value creation, though significant groundwork is still needed before that value can be realized. Overall, the Company is evaluating three potential paths forward. The path with the greatest amount of time invested to date, is at a preliminary, conceptual stage of engineering (equivalent to an AACE Class 5 to Class 4 cost estimate) and is progressing through a multi-phase metallurgical study conducted with a third party, with Phase 3 testing completed in August 2026 (metallurgical results pending). This third phase of multi-ton metallurgical work is a key milestone that should help shape next steps, with the potential to advance to a pilot plant test in Phase 4. If the tests yield positive results, it is expected the project would advance through further engineering and economic studies before any decision to execute. Early indications point to a potentially low capital intensity path for Hecla to achieve initial cash flows, though the project remains in early-stage testing and depends on the potential third-party partner securing a suitable processing facility. As an added benefit, reprocessing all or part of the existing tailings could decrease the space needed for tailings storage and help lower the mine's long-term reclamation liability. The Company is also at an early stage of evaluating two additional pathways associated with the dry-stack tailings. The first is based on advances in processing technology and growing market demand for material like Greens Creek tailings, which has created the potential to turn material once managed only as tailings into a marketable low-grade feedstock. This potential project pathway could recover additional silver and gold currently contained in tailings material, subject to further metallurgical testing and the identification of a suitable third-party processing arrangement. In the fourth quarter, we expect to load a test parcel from Greens Creek of approximately 5,500 dry metric tonnes of low-grade feedstock for shipment and sale to a third party smelter. The second option is a potential self-processing pathway that would require an onsite processing facility that could require new or amended permits. The Company expects to begin metallurgical evaluation of the self-processing concept in the first quarter of 2027, with results from this testing potentially available by spring 2027 to help determine potential next steps. The Company expects to be able to provide further details on these options in coming quarters as evaluation work advances. Potential for the combination of two or more of these three options is also being evaluated. At September 30, 2026, the dry-stack tailings facility at Greens Creek held an estimated 10.7 million tons of material, containing roughly 51 million ounces of silver, nearly 600 thousand ounces of gold, and additional critical minerals, representing a combined estimated in-situ gross metal value of approximately $6.4 billion (based on September 30, 2026 metals prices and before transportation, processing or sales costs, which are expected to be significant). This material is not a mineral resource or mineral reserve. Any recovery would depend on further testing, a suitable processing arrangement and favorable economics. Midas Restart Project Hecla continues to evaluate the potential to restart the existing Midas mill in northern Nevada, a historic high-grade gold and silver operation. Midas benefits from existing permitted infrastructure, which could help reduce the capital required for restart, and the Company is working to expand the existing high-grade gold and silver resource to the scale needed to support that restart. Midas represents a potential hub-and-spoke operating model, with ore potentially sourced from multiple regional deposits and fed into the 1,200 tpd mill. The site also includes an existing permitted tailings facility, offering approximately 15 years of storage capacity at the mill's nameplate capacity. The Company has allocated $16 million of the 2026 exploration budget for the Nevada project portfolio, more than three times the investment made in 2025. The 2026 drill program at Midas is focused on following up on the success of the 2025 drill program with a heavy focus on SE Pediment area that includes multiple targets including Sinter, Sinter Offset, and Pogo. The nearby Hollister high-grade gold and silver project is within trucking distance of the Midas mill and drilling resumed in the third quarter after a multi-year pause. With multiple veins 9 and trends still open along strike and at depth, and programs at Aurora and Hollister beginning in the third quarter, the Company expects continued exploration momentum through the fourth quarter of 2026 and aims to provide regular exploration updates for the Nevada exploration projects throughout the coming quarters.
